 eThekwini braces itself as thunderstorm looms 
 eThekwini said the warning, which is in effect until Monday evening, is particularly pertinent for residents in the metro as it is expected to be significantly affected.

 The South African Weather Service (Saws) has issued a yellow level 2 warning for severe thunderstorms that will impact multiple cities in KwaZulu-Natal, including Durban, Mooi River, and KwaDukuza. 
 eThekwini said the warning, which is in effect until Monday evening, is particularly pertinent for residents in the metro as it is expected to be significantly affected. 
 It has urged residents to take precautions as the anticipated heavy downpours, strong damaging winds, excessive lightning, and hail all pose a risk to life, property, and infrastructure.
 ALSO READ | eThekwini denies spending R1,5 million on informal housing 
 The City further cautioned residents to avoid low-lying areas, roads, and bridges that are prone to flooding and urged motorists to drive cautiously as poor visibility and slippery roads will make driving hazardous.
 Where possible, residents are encouraged to remain indoors and avoid unnecessary travel.
 The municipality said its disaster management and emergency services are on high alert should any incidents occur and encouraged people to contact the City’s Disaster Management Centre on 031 361 0000 in the case of an emergency.
 It also implored the public not to attempt crossing swollen rivers or streams during heavy rains.
 Saws said there was a high likelihood of impact across the central and eastern parts of KZN as thunderstorms are expected to intensify on Sunday and Monday.
 Potential impact includes: 
 Localised damage to infrastructure and settlements
 Localised flooding of susceptible roads and bridges
 Minor motor vehicle accidents 
 Large amounts of hail
